html:
Four days of peaceful mass protest in Manila in February 1986 that ended the twenty year rule of Ferdinand Marcos in the Philippines.

Anger had grown since the murder of Ninoy Aquino in 1983. Marcos called a snap election for February 1986, and Aquino's widow, Corazon Aquino, ran against him. The official count gave Marcos the win, but election workers walked out in protest at the fraud.

On 22 February the defence minister Juan Ponce Enrile and General Fidel Ramos broke with Marcos and barricaded themselves in two army camps on EDSA, a great avenue in Manila. Cardinal Jaime Sin called on people to protect them. Hundreds of thousands came. Nuns, priests and families knelt before tanks, offering flowers and food to soldiers, and the troops did not fire.

On 25 February Aquino was sworn in as president. That night American helicopters flew Marcos and his family out, and they went into exile in Hawaii. The revolution became a model of nonviolent change and inspired movements across Asia and the revolutions of 1989 in Europe.
sum: Four days of peaceful mass protest in Manila in February 1986 that ended the twenty year rule of Ferdinand Marcos in the Philippines.
